### An Honest Day’s Pay?
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/an-honest-day-s-pay-one-year-devotions-for-men-december-19.html
Passage: Matthew 20:13, 15
Points:
- Modern workplace debates center on fairness, but Jesus illustrates the deeper reality of divine generosity.
- The landowner honored his agreed wage with early workers while freely giving extra kindness to late arrivals.
- God treats everyone with perfect justice while adding undeserved measures of mercy as He pleases.
- Believers should rejoice that God grants eternal life rather than paying what our sins deserve.
- Christian discipleship values fair wages and honest work while keeping room for kindness and grace.

### The Principles of the Parable of the Vineyard
Author: John MacArthur
Site: Grace to You
URL: https://www.gty.org/blogs/B181207/the-principles-of-the-parable-of-the-vineyard
Passage: Matthew 20:1-15
Points:
- Salvation and eternal life are sovereign gifts of grace rather than wages earned through human labor.
- All believers receive the same gift of heaven regardless of when or how long they have served Christ.
- God initiates salvation by seeking out those who recognize their own spiritual desperation and poverty.
- The Lord unfailingly fulfills His promises and always gives far more than anyone deserves.
- Believers must never resent God's generosity toward others, but should joyfully celebrate His boundless mercy.

### The Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/parable-laborers-vineyard
Passage: Matthew 20:14-15
Points:
- A large grape harvest led the landowner to hire laborers at multiple intervals throughout the day.
- Workers hired early grumbled because those hired at the eleventh hour received the same denarius.
- The landowner maintained his sovereign right to dispense his own wealth with exceptional generosity.
- God is never unjust to anyone, always providing exactly what He has promised.
- Because fallen sinners deserve wrath rather than reward, no one can fault God for extending grace to others.
